sources.note: No prosodic statement. The numerals are transcribed with three level-tone diacritics (acute, macron, grave: e.g. 1 mōndā ~ mbírāŋ, 2 tʃírí, 3 hā̰sī, 4 ndày, 5 ndìyārá, 10 wàl, 20 wèy tʃírí), i.e. the contributor treats Besme as a tone language with at least H/M/L marking — tone MARKS in a wordlist, not a statement; nothing on stress.

sources.note: No descriptive reference for Besme (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology). Besme-tagged items are only Isaac & Roberts 1999 and Lafarge & Seignobos 1975, 1977 (ethnographic survey reports). Phonologies exist for the sister languages Kim (Lafarge 1977, 1978; Mouchet 1954) and Goundo (Roberts 1999, 2012), not for Besme.
Stubs; cite only Ethnologue and Roberts 1999 (a Goundo paper). No phonology, tone or stress information.
